paper_structure_verified: OCR Combined Science B (Twenty First Century Science) J260. Foundation: Paper 1 Biology J260/01, Paper 2 Chemistry J260/02, Paper 3 Physics J260/03, each 95 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 26.4% of the GCSE; Paper 4 Combined Science J260/04, 75 marks, 1 hour 45 minutes, 20.8%. Higher mirrors this as Papers 5-8 (J260/05-08) with the same marks and timings. Paper 1 (and Paper 5) assesses B1-B6 plus BCP7 and BCP8; Paper 4 (and Paper 8) assesses all content. Higher-tier-only statements are shown in bold type. Practical work is the Practical Activity Groups (PAG).

findings.claim: A higher-only block opens 'At higher tier, you may be asked about non-coding DNA.'
findings.truth: B1.1 has no bold statements, so nothing in it is Higher tier only, and 'non-coding DNA', transcription, translation, mRNA, triplet and ribosome appear nowhere in J260. The tier claim is false and the content is enrichment, not assessed. Wrapper removed and the sentence reworded to say it is background.
findings.evidence: spec B1.1 outcomes 1-6, none bold in combined-science-b-21c-J260-bold.md; tiering rule 'Statements shown in bold type will only be tested in the Higher Tier papers'; grep of the spec returns no hit for non-coding / mRNA / transcription / translation / triplet / ribosome

findings.claim: The whole 'Polydactyly - A Dominant Inherited Condition' section sits inside a higher-only wrapper.
findings.truth: B1.2 contains no bold statements. Outcome B1.2.2 'explain single gene inheritance, including dominant and recessive alleles and use of genetic diagrams' and B1.2.3 'predict the results of single gene crosses' are assessed at both tiers, so a Foundation student must meet a dominant-allele cross. The wrapper hid both-tier content; removed.
findings.evidence: spec B1.2 outcomes 1-7, none bold in combined-science-b-21c-J260-bold.md

findings.claim: Item 1 asks for the genotype of a carrier. Options are FF, Ff, ff, fF, with 'Ff' keyed correct.
findings.truth: 'fF' and 'Ff' name the same heterozygous genotype, so the item had two correct options and marked a true answer wrong. Option 4 replaced with 'Either FF or ff'.
findings.evidence: settled fact: allele order in a genotype carries no meaning; both strings mean one dominant and one recessive allele

findings.claim: 'In 2001, a couple discovered through genetic testing that they had both inherited the allele for Huntington's disease - a dominant, inherited condition...'
findings.truth: The same sentence calls the condition dominant, so one copy is enough to cause it. Saying both partners carry the allele contradicts the lesson and suggests a dominant condition needs two affected parents. Changed to 'one of them had inherited'.
findings.evidence: settled fact plus the lesson's own words 'a dominant, inherited condition'; spec B1.2.1 'explain the terms ... dominant and recessive'

findings.claim: The lesson covers genetic testing, embryo screening, gene therapy, GM crops and ethics.
findings.truth: B1.3.3 is bold, so it is Higher tier only, and it is taught nowhere in this unit: 'describe the main steps in the process of genetic engineering including: isolating and replicating the required gene(s); putting the gene(s) into a vector (e.g. a plasmid); using the vector to insert the gene(s) into cells; selecting modified cells'. Options: add a short higher-only block to L3 covering the four steps (needs new narration ids, so it cannot be a surgical edit), or accept the gap and log it for a rebuild.
findings.evidence: spec B1.3 outcome 3, bold in combined-science-b-21c-J260-bold.md

findings.claim: A full section, two knowledge checks, two practice questions and three flashcards cover somatic and germline gene therapy.
findings.truth: 'gene therapy' does not appear anywhere in J260. It is defensible only as an example under B1.3.4 (benefits and risks of gene technology in medicine). Not wrong, but it carries more weight in the lesson than the spec gives it, while the assessed genetic-engineering steps are absent (see F5).
findings.evidence: grep of specs/ocr/combined-science-b-21c-J260.md returns no hit for 'gene therapy'

findings.claim: 'athlete's foot is caused by Tinea fungi'
findings.truth: Tinea is the name of the infection, not the fungus. The fungi are dermatophytes such as Trichophyton. The spec asks only for 'Athlete's foot (fungal)', so no marks turn on this.
findings.evidence: spec B2.1.4 names 'Athlete's foot (fungal)' without naming an organism

findings.claim: The opening vignette states that in the same communities as the 2018-19 European measles outbreaks, 'adults were being diagnosed with type 2 diabetes at record rates'.
findings.truth: The measles half is sound. The diabetes half is an unsourced claim about the same communities and cannot be checked. It is framing, not assessed content, so it is left alone.
findings.evidence: no spec or settled-fact basis either way

findings.claim: Flashcard 12 asks 'Name one way antibodies destroy pathogens other than by binding to the antigen.' The keyed answer is agglutination.
findings.truth: Every antibody action begins with the antibody binding to the antigen, agglutination included, so the question asked for something that does not exist and its own answer breaks its condition. Reworded to 'Name one way antibodies help to destroy pathogens.'
findings.evidence: spec B2.2 narrative: 'An antibody is specific for (only binds to) a particular antigen'

findings.claim: The paragraph naming the three factors, defining 'limiting factor' and explaining the graph plateau is wrapped in higher-only.
findings.truth: B3.1.4a 'explain the effect of temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration on the rate of photosynthesis' is not bold, so it is tested at both tiers. The wrapper also hid the only <dfn> for 'limiting factor', a term used throughout the rest of the lesson, the key facts and the conclusion. Wrapper removed.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1 outcome 4a not bold; outcomes 5 and 6 bold, in combined-science-b-21c-J260-bold.md

findings.claim: Item 2 asks what a plateau on a rate-against-light-intensity graph means, untagged.
findings.truth: Reading the interaction of the three factors off a graph is B3.1.6, which is bold and therefore Higher tier only. Prefixed '(Higher tier)'.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1 outcome 6 (bold): 'explain the interaction of temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration in limiting the rate of photosynthesis, and use graphs depicting the effects'

findings.claim: Question 3 asks why a tomato plant in a sealed glasshouse stops speeding up even when given more light, untagged.
findings.truth: One factor limiting the rate while another is raised is the interaction in B3.1.6, which is Higher tier only. Prefixed '(Higher tier)'.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1 outcome 6 (bold)

findings.claim: Item 5 stem: 'Match each mineral ion to the molecule it helps produce in plants:' with nitrate ions, phosphate ions and CO2 as the three items.
findings.truth: Carbon dioxide is a gas, not a mineral ion. The stem taught a wrong classification. Stem changed to 'Match each substance...'. The three pairings themselves are right.
findings.evidence: spec B3.2 narrative: 'Producers get nitrogen from nitrate ions (NO3-)'; carbon dioxide is listed separately as a gas that moves by diffusion

findings.claim: Question 1 is typed '1 mark - State/Name' and its key reads 'Glucose [1] and oxygen [1]. Both must be stated for the mark. (1 mark for both...)'.
findings.truth: Two [1] tags on a one-mark question contradict the sentence that follows. Rewritten as a single mark for both products.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction in the key

findings.claim: Question 5 (Plot A high light and CO2 but low nitrate, Plot B low light but high nitrate) keys Plot A, reasoning 'Low nitrate will limit protein synthesis but plants can still photosynthesise and store starch'.
findings.truth: The lesson's own text says 'A shortage of any of these resources limits growth regardless of how much light or CO2 is available', and a nitrogen shortage lowers chlorophyll and enzyme levels, so it lowers the photosynthetic rate itself, not just protein synthesis. The key and the article contradicted each other. Rekeyed to Plot B with the nitrate-to-chlorophyll-and-enzyme link spelled out; the question stem is unchanged.
findings.evidence: lesson content_html paragraph n17; spec B3.2 narrative 'The way in which photosynthetic organisms take in nitrogen (to make proteins)'

findings.claim: After F10 the remaining Higher-tier-only material in this lesson carries no tier flag: the key fact 'The three limiting factors interact... a graph plateau means a different factor is now limiting', the collapsible 'How Each Factor Limits the Rate', the second conclusion bullet and the exam tip. Separately, B3.1.5 is absent.
findings.truth: B3.1.6 (interaction and graphs) and B3.1.5 (use the inverse square law to explain why the rate changes with distance from a light source) are both bold, so both are Higher tier only. The lesson only says 'If a plant is moved further from a light source, the light reaching it decreases' - no inverse square law at all. Options: wrap the key fact and the conclusion bullet in higher-only and add an inverse-square-law block (new narration ids needed), or leave the prose open to both tiers and rely on the question tags in F11/F12. Recommend adding the inverse square law in a rebuild and leaving the prose open.
findings.evidence: spec B3.1 outcomes 5 and 6, both bold

findings.claim: Question 1 is typed '1 mark - State/Name' and its key reads 'One mark for any correct biotic factor ... AND one mark for any correct abiotic factor ... Both required for the mark.'
findings.truth: The key awards two marks and then calls it one. Rewritten as a single mark that needs both factors.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction in the key

findings.claim: 'In the late 1980s, scientists tracking red fox populations across the Scottish Highlands noticed... as foxes declined... mountain hares surged, only to crash again as overgrazing damaged the heather'.
findings.truth: The ecology described is sound and mountain hare numbers in Scotland do cycle, but no study of that date and place is identifiable. It reads as reportage of a specific study. Left alone because the claim cannot be shown false and nothing assessed rests on it.
findings.evidence: no spec basis; not a settled fact either way

findings.claim: The unit is named 'biology-paper-1' and a sibling unit 'science-ocr-b/biology-paper-2' is queued, implying two biology papers.
findings.truth: J260 has ONE biology paper: J260/01 at Foundation and J260/05 at Higher, and it assesses chapters B1-B6 plus BCP7 and BCP8. Paper 2 (J260/02 F, J260/06 H) is chemistry, Paper 3 (J260/03, J260/07) is physics and Paper 4 (J260/04, J260/08) assesses all content. Two-biology-paper naming is Gateway-shaped and does not exist in this specification. Verified lesson-to-chapter mapping for this unit: L1 = B1.1, L2 = B1.2, L3 = B1.3, L4 = B2.1 and part of B2.2, L5 = B2.2, B2.3 and B2.5, L6 = B2.4 and B2.5, L7 = B3.1 and B3.2, L8 = B3.3, B3.4 and the biodiversity part of B6.3. The unit therefore covers B1-B3 only. Options: rename the two units by chapter range (B1-B3 / B4-B6) or as 'part 1 / part 2', or keep the slugs and fix only the display titles. Recommend renaming the display titles by chapter range; no lesson text asserts a paper structure, so no lesson edits follow.
findings.evidence: spec assessment overview: 'Paper 1 assesses content B1-B6 and BCP7 and 8'; J260/01 95 marks 1 hour 45 minutes 26.4%; J260/04 75 marks 1 hour 45 minutes 20.8%; Higher mirror J260/05-08

findings.claim: Eight lessons are presented as the coverage of B1-B3.
findings.truth: Assessable outcomes in B1-B3 that are taught nowhere in this unit (the sibling unit covers B4-B6, so these are real gaps, not deferrals): B1.1.1a/1b nucleus, plasmids and light-microscope use; B1.3.3 genetic-engineering steps (Higher only); B2.1.5 plant diseases (tobacco mosaic virus, ash dieback, crown gall); B2.2.1 microbial defences and B2.2.2 platelets; B2.3.1 prevention in plants (polyculture, crop rotation, biological control); B2.5.2 clear-zone area calculations with pi r squared; B3.1.3 enzyme action, lock and key, and the effect of substrate concentration, temperature and pH; B3.1.5 inverse square law (Higher only); B3.2.2-3.2.5 diffusion, osmosis, root hair cells, xylem and phloem structure; B3.3.7-3.3.8 carbon and water cycles and the role of microorganisms in decomposition; B3.4.2 field investigation of distribution and abundance. No Practical Activity Group (PAGB1 to PAGB5) is described anywhere in the unit. Options: extend the unit, or accept the gaps and record them on the subject build plan.
findings.evidence: spec chapters B1-B3 assessable learning outcomes, cross-checked against all eight raw lesson files

summary: Eight lessons read against J260. Twelve edits fix three wrong higher-only wrappers (L1, L2, L7), a knowledge check with two correct options (L2 Ff/fF), a dominant-allele contradiction in the Huntington's vignette (L3), an impossible flashcard question (L5), CO2 called a mineral ion (L7), two self-contradicting one-mark keys (L7, L8) and two Higher-tier question tags. A thirteenth edit rekeys the L7 Plot A / Plot B question to Plot B (F15, approved by the coordinator) so the key agrees with the lesson's limiting-factor statement. Four items need adjudication: the missing Higher-only genetic-engineering steps, the untagged Higher material and missing inverse square law in L7, and, at unit level, the Gateway-shaped 'biology-paper-1/2' naming plus a long list of B1-B3 outcomes and every PAG that this unit never teaches.
